items.title: Amos White Interview, 1958-08-23
items.q: But I went down there because I had a friend down there. And I still consider her one of my greatest friends. But she is so, she's such a devout Catholic and a good Christian person. That's right. And it would be shameless for me to say anything different about her. She befriended me so many times.

ctx.x: Yeah, sure. Yeah, sure. And so, when we walked in, I said, I'm reporting from the 816th Finan Enfrager on the orders of Colonel Chaplin to come up here and serenade you. He said, hell, we don't need any serenading up here. I'll do it to serenade. He said, go on back there and get you something to eat and you can go on back to camp. Oh, he's a wonderful guy, you know. That's why I love him until today. He was so forthright. Great man. But, back to the regiment of band activities. Now, when they started building…
By the way, Lizzie's coming out here to Monterey and I guess next month. Is she?

items.title: Lizzie Miles Interview, 1951-01-18
items.q: I think there was a piano, either banjo or a guitar, cornet, Amos White was playing the cornet. He's now in Oakland, California, Amos White, cornet player.

ctx.x: Who was in the band? Who else?

Well, now I see, there was Manuel Mineta and there was, um, I can't, I can't, I think, I think Carrie Fritz was the, I think Carrie was the cornet player. And, um, they had a cornet, I think banjo or guitar, I'm not sure, I can't remember so well. But, um, I think there was a piano, either banjo or a guitar, cornet, Amos White was playing the cornet. He's now in Oakland, California, Amos White, cornet player. He was cornet and they had drums and trombone and manual on the piano.
